title: Boutique Hotel Desk

spec.useCase: Evangeline Prescott-Adeyemi owns an inn and uses this to see who arrives and leaves today, which rooms are ready, what is waiting to be cleaned and which repairs are open.

text.text: Run the inn from one page: rooms and their state, reservations with nights and totals, today's cleaning and the repairs that cannot wait. Start the day on the Dashboard and Arriving today, then work Mine. Never mark a room Ready until the cleaning job has passed inspection.

Nights multiplied by the room rate
Quote this to the guest and note any package or discount
Nights of stays beginning this month
Compare against room count times days to see occupancy
Repairs Reported or Scheduled for the room

text.text: Welcome note, towels and amenities in place
Requests read: allergies, dietary needs, occasions
Greet by name and confirm the stay dates.
Explain breakfast, parking, quiet hours and the Wi-Fi.
Press Check in guest on the reservation.
Ask about the stay and thank them.
Press Check out guest, then create a cleaning job for the room.
The first and last five minutes decide the review.
Dust high to low and wipe all surfaces.
Clean the bathroom top to bottom; polish fixtures.
Make the bed with fresh linens and fold towels.
Vacuum or mop and check under beds.
A second person checks each turnover before the room is marked Ready.
Anything broken becomes a repair row, not a note on a paper.
Do stay-over service by midday; leave a card with the option to skip it.
Walk the building with the Repairs view open.
Check smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; test hot water in one room per day.
Any repair that affects safety goes to Urgent and the room is set to Out of service until it is fixed.
Read tomorrow's reservations for dietary needs and arrival times.
Prepare the breakfast prep list with counts.
Check allergies against the menu before service.
Serve on time; offer a take-away option for early departures.
Log guest feedback in the reservation.
Write down every request in the reservation, and tick it off once it is done. Surprises are best when they are planned.
